notes: §1985:XIII.4.9.3 SR3 has two sentences: GENERATE, INITIATE or TERMINATE 'must not appear in a paragraph within a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure', and 'A PERFORM statement in a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure must not have GENERATE, INITIATE, or TERMINATE statements in its range.' The first is ReportWriterBinder#RejectInBeforeReporting over EnclosingContext#InBeforeReportingProcedure, read by BindGenerate/BindInitiate/BindTerminate at every edition (COBOL2378, the witness). The second has no site at --std 85: 2023 replaced it with the run-time EC-FLOW-REPORT of §2023:14.9.49.4 GR10, and no 1985 edition arm restores the compile-time refusal. Probes at --std 85 (class b each statement and the PERFORM arm; class c the 2023 run-time relaxation): GENERATE, INITIATE, TERMINATE and a TERMINATE nested in IF inside the UBR paragraph each refused COBOL2378; PERFORM ERR-PARA and PERFORM ERR-USE (a USE AFTER ERROR section whose paragraph holds GENERATE DL or INITIATE RPT) compile rc=0 and run, printing DONE with the report TITLE/LINE (the performed GENERATE silently does nothing); the legal UBR (ADD/DISPLAY) prints PH 1. Classes a, d, e, f do not apply. kb/Work PB5254 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-pipe/slice-56.json).

next.reason: 1985: "A PERFORM statement in a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure must not have GENERATE, INITIATE, or TERMINATE statements in its range."; 2023: "If a GENERATE, INITIATE, or TERMINATE statement is executed within the range of a declarative ... EC-FLOW-REPORT ... is set". The paragraph ban is kept verbatim. The PERFORM-range ban is no longer a syntax rule: execution in the range is defined as unsuccessful and sets EC-FLOW-REPORT.
